hero.title: Digital Marketing Manager Resume Skills: *100+ skills* for your resume
hero.lede: The digital marketing skills hiring managers and ATS actually scan for in 2026 — SEO, paid media, content, social, email, and the analytics that prove ROI. Organized by channel and experience level, with real examples of how to phrase them. Explore the list, or generate a set tailored to you.

quickAnswer.question: What skills should a digital marketing manager put on a resume?
quickAnswer.answer: Show breadth across channels plus proof you drive results. Cover the acquisition mix — SEO, PPC/Google Ads, content, social, and email — then the analytics that prove it worked: Google Analytics, conversion tracking, and ROI. Add the strategy and leadership that make you a manager, not just a specialist, and name the platforms you run campaigns in. Tailor the exact mix to the channels the role prioritizes.

mistakes.title: Listing channels with no results.
mistakes.detail: “SEO” and “social media” mean little alone — back them with traffic, leads, or ROI.

mistakes.title: No analytics skills.
mistakes.detail: Managers are judged on ROI. Google Analytics and conversion tracking are must-haves.

mistakes.title: All execution, no strategy.
mistakes.detail: For a manager role, show you set direction and own budget, not just run campaigns.

mistakes.title: Buzzword soup.
mistakes.detail: “Guru”, “ninja”, “rockstar” read as filler. Use the actual skill names recruiters scan for.

mistakes.title: Ignoring the budget you managed.
mistakes.detail: Ad spend and team size signal scope — quantify what you were responsible for.

mistakes.title: One channel only.
mistakes.detail: Manager roles want an integrated mix. Show breadth even if you have a specialty.

skillsToAvoid.heading: Skills you usually don't need to list
skillsToAvoid.description: For modern digital marketing manager roles these are assumed or too generic — including them dilutes your stronger skills. Leave them off unless a specific posting explicitly asks.

faq.q: How many skills should a digital marketing manager put on a resume?
faq.a: Aim for 14–18 skills that show breadth across channels plus analytics and strategy. Enough to prove you can run an integrated mix, but curated to what you can back with results. If you have a specialty (say, paid or SEO), lead with it while still showing range.

faq.q: What are the most important digital marketing skills?
faq.a: SEO, PPC/Google Ads, content marketing, social media, and email are the core channels, and Google Analytics with conversion tracking is the non-negotiable measurement layer. For a manager role, add strategy, budget management, and leadership to show you direct the mix, not just execute one part of it.

faq.q: Do digital marketers need analytics and data skills?
faq.a: Yes — analytics is now central to the role. Google Analytics (GA4), Google Tag Manager, conversion tracking, and ROI/attribution analysis appear in most job descriptions because employers hire marketers who can prove impact, not just run campaigns. List them prominently.

faq.q: Should I list specific tools like HubSpot and SEMrush?
faq.a: Yes — platform names are keywords recruiters and ATS scan for. List the ones you genuinely use: HubSpot or Mailchimp for automation, SEMrush or Ahrefs for SEO, Google Ads and Meta Business Suite for paid. Depth in a few beats naming every tool you've opened once.

faq.q: What skills should a junior digital marketer include?
faq.a: Focus on hands-on channel skills you can demonstrate: SEO basics, running Google Ads or social campaigns, email marketing, copywriting, and Google Analytics. Back each with a real campaign and its numbers. At entry level, evidence you moved a metric beats claiming full strategy ownership.

faq.q: How do I show ROI on a marketing resume?
faq.a: Pair each channel skill with a quantified outcome: traffic growth, cost-per-acquisition reduced, conversion rate lifted, pipeline or revenue generated, and the budget you managed. Numbers turn a list of channels into evidence you drive business results — which is what hiring managers filter for.

faq.q: How do I tailor marketing skills to a job description?
faq.a: Read the posting and note which channels it prioritizes (paid vs organic vs lifecycle), the tools it names, and whether it's execution- or strategy-focused. Mirror those in your own true words and move them toward the top, since ATS ranks you partly on how well your resume echoes the job's language.
